paper_metadata.title: Effects of Cold Rolling and Annealing Treatment on Microstructure and Properties of CoFeNiMnV High-Entropy Alloys

evidence.quote: Herein, a combination of cold rolling (CR) and annealing treatment is used to investigate the evolution of the microstructure and mechanical properties of CoFeNiMnV high-entropy alloys (HEAs) fabricated by powder plasma arc additive manufacturing (PPA-AM).
The significant increase in the strength of CoFeNiMnV HEAs after rolling can be attributed to grain boundary strengthening due to dislocation strengthening and grain refinement.

The experimental deposition parameters are shown in Table 1 .
High-purity argon (99.9% purity) was used as protective gas, ion gas, and powder feed gas during the deposition process.
The metal powder and alumina (metal powder and grinding ball mass ratio of 1:2) grinding ball were put into the high-energy ball mill for 6 h of grinding experiment.
After grinding, the metal powder was wrapped in tinfoil and placed in a vacuum-drying oven to dry for 3 h.

The CoFeNiMnV HEAs samples were subjected to multipass rolling with small deformation in the rolling direction (RD, travel direction) using a roll with a diameter of 180 mm (M180 experimental rolling mill) at room temperature. The rolling amount was 50%, and the ﬁnal thickness after CR was 10 mm.

Figure 2 shows the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of the PPA-AM deposited, cold rolled, and annealed CoFeNiMnV HEAs, from which it can be conﬁrmed that the CoFeNiMnV HEAs form the FCC solid solution phase.
The grains of HEA-Depositing are relatively coarse (Figure 3a), and there are σ phases (gray-black area) dispersed in the gray FCC matrix and between the grain boundaries.
As seen in Figure 5a, the HEA-depositing sample exhibits elongated and coarse grain characteristics, which are the cross-sectional morphology of columnar grains.
The XRD patterns show that the alloys of CoFeNiMnV HEAs have no phase transformation after rolling and annealing.
After 50% CR deformation, the grains of CR-HEA are deformed along the RD direction, and the grains are re ﬁned.
The microstructure of the CR-HEA was mainly composed of subgrains, with a fraction of LAGBs of 92.83% and HAGBs of 6.94%.

There are a large number of high angle grain boundaries (HAGBs) ( /C25 92.19%) and a small amount of low angle grain boundaries (LAGBs) in the HEA-depositing sample, and there are almost no twins.
At 700 °C, both recrystallized grains (26.35%) and nonrecrystallized grains are observed in the microstructure (Figure 7d).
In this state, a small number of annealing twins are generated, and the proportion of twins is /C25 6.09%.
With the annealing temperature rising to 900 °C, the alloy has almost completely recrystallized (Figure 5e). The recrystallized grain and twin size of the alloy are further coarsened
The grain boundaries of the alloy are mainly composed of HAGBs and twins, and the proportion of annealing twins is greatly increased to 31.17% (Figure 5e1).

The direct deposition sample (Figure 7a) is not deformed, there is almost no dislocation in the structure, and the proportion of the recrystallized structure accounts for /C25 98.69% of the main part.
After 50% CR deformation, slip dislocations accumulate and entangle, resulting in a sharp increase in LAGBs.
The recrystallized grain and twin size of the alloy are further coarsened, and the dislocation density continues to decrease, resulting in the almost disappearance of LAGBs in the alloy crystal.
